posts.text: The minimum wage isn't really frozen at $7.25. A new Cato paper finds that counting state and local floors, the effective minimum Americans face has risen to $12.13, higher than at most points in recent history. Instituting a much higher federal minimum would override local choices and bite hardest where wages are lowest, explain Cato’s Ryan Bourne and Nathan Miller.
